chapter_title: Which Summer Job Pays 1500 a Day?

segments.title: Which Summer Job Pays 1500 a Day?
segments.content:
On the evening after the high school entrance exams ended, Li Luo sat in a chair in Ying Chanxi's study, turned on her family's computer, and stared at the screen, engrossed.

He skillfully typed in his QQ account number and logged into his QQ from twenty years ago.

At this time, his friends list only contained classmates from elementary and middle school.

It was foreseeable that in this life, he would likely never meet his high school and college classmates from his past life again.

At the very least, they were unlikely to appear in his friends list again.

After the high school entrance exams, his life had already started down a path completely different from his previous life.

Sighing softly, Li Luo opened a web browser and searched Baidu for a host of well-known websites.

This era could be described as the turning point when the internet gradually transitioned from the PC to the mobile age.

In film and television, Tencent Video, iQiyi, and Youku Tudou were still at each other's throats, fighting for market share.

Live-streaming platforms were also popping up like mushrooms after rain; Douyu, Huya, and others were all making their mark during this period.

Offline, three food delivery platforms vied for dominance: Meituan, Ele.me, and Baidu Waimai were all scrambling for a piece of the pie.

In the ride-hailing sector, Didi and Kuaidi were also in a heated back-and-forth battle.

The dust of the mobile internet war had not yet settled as it had in later years.

However, regarding these matters, even the reborn Li Luo could only watch from the sidelines.

Whether it was the 35-year-old Li Luo or the 15-year-old Li Luo, he was just an ordinary person.

He had no capital, no connections, and certainly no extraordinary abilities.

While the memory palace ability was good, it was limited by his mental and physical energy and was not omnipotent.

So, after scrolling through the familiar names on the web pages with some excitement, Li Luo's heart gradually cooled down, returning to a state of calm.

Although behind the dazzling array of names on the screen lay endless streams of money and wealth.

These things, whether before or after his rebirth, most likely had nothing to do with him.

He felt his pants pocket; he only had just over thirty yuan in allowance. Factoring in his underage status, he couldn't even buy stocks...

After thinking this through, Li Luo sighed and abandoned the grand blueprints that had been swirling in his mind since his rebirth.

He had really read too many rebirth novels in his past life. He was just a struggling office worker. The most reliable thing he could do was follow the trend and find a way to persuade his parents to buy a house!

Other than that, he could only try to find a way to earn some small money first.

After all, in this day and age, almost every industry required some initial investment to succeed.

For ventures that truly had zero cost and zero barriers to entry and could still make money, apart from honest labor, there really weren't many options.

Thinking of this, Li Luo opened Baidu again and searched for two websites.

One was Bilibili, the other was Qidian Chinese Website.

Unfortunately, it was still a long time before Douyin would be launched, otherwise Li Luo would have been more inclined to look for it.

He didn't have any grander ideas right now. He just hoped his family could live without worrying about food and clothing, and then he could have a pleasant high school life.

As for making real money, that could wait until he went to university.

...

"What are you looking at?" At a little past nine in the evening, Ying Chanxi's voice suddenly came from behind Li Luo.

Her head peeked out from over Li Luo's right shoulder, her long, loose hair brushing against his cheek. It slid over his shoulder and landed on his chest.

"Why are you reading novels all of a sudden?"

"Oh... just browsing." Inhaling the faint fragrance of her hair, Li Luo glanced at Ying Chanxi. Seeing she was already in her panda pajamas, he knew she must have already taken a shower.

Then he came back to his senses and continued to scroll through the novel website on the computer screen, briefly looking over the rankings.

I Shall Seal the Heavens, Perfect World, The Desolate Era, Soul Land 2... all of them were quite ancient titles.

Li Luo was in a daze for a moment. He never thought that one day he would be able to return to a time when these books were still being serialized.

"You're not playing games today, you're reading novels instead?" Ying Chanxi asked curiously.

"Do you read them?"

"I don't." Ying Chanxi shook her head. "I still have to study the first-year high school material. I don't have time for leisure reading."

"You're too much of a grinder..."

"What does that mean?"

"Er... it means I'm complimenting you on how hardworking you are."

Ying Chanxi didn't think much of it. She leaned closer to the computer to check the time, then said, "You can play until ten o'clock at the latest, then you have to go back."

"Got it."

"I'm going to bed then."

"Okay, go ahead."

"So... good night?" Ying Chanxi blinked, looking at the computer screen instead of Li Luo's face, and spoke in a carefully inquisitive tone.

"Yeah, good night."

Hearing Li Luo's response, the corners of Ying Chanxi's mouth curled up slightly. She then turned and walked out of the study, her slippers padding softly as she returned to her bedroom.

Folding the small blanket Li Luo had personally given her when they were kids into a rectangle, she placed it on her pillow. Ying Chanxi lay down on the bed, and inhaling the scent from it, she soon drifted peacefully into dreamland.

Meanwhile, Li Luo, who was checking websites in the study, watched as the time ticked closer to ten o'clock. He then punctually shut down the computer and went back across the hall to sleep.

...

The next day, just past three in the morning.

While the sky was still dark and hazy, the couple Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong had already woken up on time, getting up in the dark.

The two of them washed up quietly to avoid waking their son, preparing to head out to the breakfast shop to start their prep work.

But just then, Li Luo's bedroom door opened.

Li Luo, already dressed, walked out. He familiarly squeezed into the bathroom, reaching between the two of them for his toothbrush and cup. "Excuse me, excuse me, I need to brush my teeth too."

"What are you up to, kid?" Lin Xiuhong looked at her son with astonishment. "It's three in the morning, why aren't you sleeping? Where are you planning to run off to and mess around so early?"

"To work a summer job," Li Luo said muffledly, after wetting his toothbrush, applying toothpaste, and stuffing it into his mouth.

Li Guohong raised an eyebrow. "Why the sudden thought of getting a summer job? It's not like your mom doesn't give you pocket money."

"What summer job are you going to work?" Lin Xiuhong also said. "Go back to sleep. I'll give you a thousand yuan for the summer break, just don't spend it recklessly."

"I'm already up, how can I fall back asleep?" Li Luo finished rinsing his mouth with a gurgle, washed his face with cold water, and dried it before following his parents out the door. "Let's go, let's go, time to set off!"

Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong walked out of their home in a daze, watching as Li Luo followed them all the way to the breakfast shop they rented across from their residential community.

Then Li Luo put on an apron and, alongside them, started cleaning the dining tables in the shop and preparing the food for the morning.

Watching their son work so diligently in the shop, the couple felt a bit dazed for a moment.

The key thing was that the kid wasn't actually getting in the way.

Things like washing and prepping vegetables were one thing, but he even learned how to make steamed buns and baozi after just being shown once.

With the three of them preparing the ingredients together, a process that would normally take until around 5:30 AM was completely finished before 5:00 AM with Li Luo's help.

All they had to do was wait for the customers to arrive.

"Alright, alright, we're all done." Lin Xiuhong pulled Li Luo over to a chair. "Rest for a bit, then go home and catch up on sleep."

"I'm not sleepy," Li Luo said, looking at his mom strangely. "I can just go back for a nap after lunch, can't I?"

"Really not sleepy?"

"Really not!" Li Luo said with a laugh. Just then, he saw an uncle walk into the shop and immediately stood up to greet him. "Uncle, what would you like? The baozi, mantou, and pan-fried dumplings still need a bit more time, but everything else is ready."

"Do you have fried noodles?"

"We do."

"Then add an egg, no spice."

"You got it." Li Luo acknowledged, then called towards the kitchen, "Dad! One order of fried noodles with an egg! No spice!"

The uncle sat down on a chair, looked at Li Luo, then at Lin Xiuhong, and asked with a smile, "Is this your son?"

"Yes, yes." Lin Xiuhong replied with a smile. "He just finished his entrance exams. I don't know what got into him, he couldn't sit still at home, so he came over to help out."

"What a sensible young man," the uncle praised. "Your family's upbringing is clearly good. My daughter... tsk tsk... she's such a headache. If only she were as sensible as your boy."

"Oh... he's just okay," Lin Xiuhong said humbly and politely. "He used to be very mischievous."

"Boys will be boys, they're all mischievous when they're young," the uncle said, shaking his head with a chuckle. He then asked, "Boss lady, do you have soy milk? Sweet soy milk, and hot, please."

"Yes, yes, I'll get it for you." Lin Xiuhong responded and was about to turn to ladle the soy milk.

But Li Luo had already scooped up a bowl of hot, sweet soy milk and handed it directly to Lin Xiuhong.

Lin Xiuhong took it, looked down at the bowl of soy milk in her hands, and unconsciously froze for a second before coming back to her senses and hurriedly serving it to the customer.

Li Luo's family's breakfast shop had been in business for over a decade, and its business was now excellent.

People from the two or three surrounding residential communities, in particular, would always choose their shop for breakfast.

From just before six in the morning until around nine-thirty, a steady stream of customers flowed through the shop.

Normally, with just the two of them, the couple Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong would often be rushed off their feet.

But today was exceptionally different from usual.

With Li Luo's help, although it was still very busy, the entire operation ran in an orderly rhythm.

The young man Li Luo bustled about, exclusively responsible for taking customer orders and then calling out to his parents to prepare the food.

With his memory palace, no matter how many customers came, Li Luo never mixed up an order and was always able to serve the food accurately, showing no signs of being flustered.

This made things much easier for Lin Xiuhong, who usually had to manage the accounts and payments while also handling the baozi, pan-fried dumplings, and fried dough sticks.

In addition, many of the customers were regulars. Seeing a new face in the shop, they couldn't help but ask about him.

Upon learning it was Lin Xiuhong's son, they would smile and offer a few words of praise.

As a result, Lin Xiuhong didn't feel tired at all; instead, she was all smiles the entire morning.

After nine o'clock, the shop wasn't as crowded, and things became a little more relaxed.

Although it was called a breakfast shop, it was actually open all day.

It was just that these few morning hours were the busiest. After midday, there were basically very few customers.

In the afternoon, they would tidy up the shop, serve a small wave of customers around five or six in the evening, and then they could close up and go home.

Having finished the morning rush, Li Luo stretched his limbs at the shop's entrance.

Although he was quite tired, he didn't feel that soul-deep exhaustion he used to feel after turning thirty.

His back didn't ache, his neck didn't hurt, and he was still full of energy.

This 15-year-old body truly is something else!

Li Luo felt the sweat trickle down his forehead with a look of satisfaction, feeling that everything was just wonderful.

Just then, Li Guohong was cleaning the kitchen when he heard quiet sobs from behind him.

He turned his head to see Lin Xiuhong hiding in a corner, secretly wiping away tears.

"Hey, what are you crying for?" Li Guohong walked over, put a hand on his wife's shoulder, and passed her a tissue.

"It's nothing... I'm just happy..." Lin Xiuhong cried and laughed at the same time, wiping her tears. She choked a couple of times, patted her chest, and said to Li Guohong, "Do you think Li Luo has grown up? It feels like he's become sensible all of a sudden. I'm so happy today, you have no idea how many people praised him this morning."

"That's a good thing." Li Guohong smiled too, hugging Lin Xiuhong. "Li Luo has become sensible, we should just be happy. He's a boy, I've said it before, he'll grow up eventually."

"Yes, you're right." Lin Xiuhong, with tears still in the corners of her eyes, smiled with exceptional joy. She then walked to the counter, took out a stack of red banknotes from inside, and began to count.

"What's this for?"

"His pocket money for the summer break," Lin Xiuhong said as she counted, then pulled out ten of Grandpa Mao's bills.

But her hand paused, and she pulled out five more, a total of 1500 yuan, clenching it in her palm.

After wiping the tear stains from the corners of her eyes, Lin Xiuhong took a deep breath, composed herself, and walked out of the kitchen to Li Luo's side.

She looked up at her son, who was already 1.75 meters tall, and her mind flashed back to his rebellious behavior a few years ago.

Then the memory shifted to the past few days, leaving Lin Xiuhong in a daze.

"Mom, what's wrong?" Li Luo looked at Lin Xiuhong strangely and waved a hand in front of her face. "Are you tired?"

"No, I'm not tired." Lin Xiuhong shook her head, coming back to her senses. She reached out, took Li Luo's hand, and pressed the fifteen bright red banknotes into his palm. "Take it. It's summer break, so have fun. Once you start high school, you'll have to work hard."

Li Luo looked down at the money in his hand, blinked, and then took a deep breath.

He vaguely remembered that during this same summer break in his previous life, he had argued with his parents because he went to play basketball the day before the exam.

He also didn't do well on the exam.

In the end, he didn't get a single cent of pocket money.

And now, the exam results weren't even out yet... He had only acted like a normal student doing normal things and helped out a bit at the shop...

And he was handed 1500 yuan in pocket money.

Back when he was in university, his monthly living expenses were only about that much.

Emotions churned inside Li Luo, but what he said was, "Mom, is the summer job here that profitable? Can I come again tomorrow? For a gig that pays 1500 a day, I could work it until I retire."

"..." Lin Xiuhong stared at this boy who couldn't say anything nice, all her heartfelt emotion instantly vanishing. "Get the hell out of here!"
